plotSections.title: The Doorman and the Gatekeepers
bullets: Gerk is formally recognized as an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Tree. He is specifically distinguished from the others as the Doorman, while the rest of the party are Gatekeepers.

Gerk discovers that being the Doorman grants him the ability to open a door directly through reality. He reaches for an invisible handle and opens a seamless doorway onto an unknown coastline on Midgard at sunset.
The door does not appear as a conventional portal; Gerk effectively peels reality back, creating a standard-width doorway with no visible threshold between the current location and the destination.
The exact destination of Gerk's door cannot currently be chosen reliably. The DM only knows that the first destination was somewhere on Midgard, apparently along a coastline.
Sylan attempts to use his keystone to open a passage but only briefly feels something in the air before it disappears. He concludes that he will need more time to work with the keystone.

The distinction between Gerk's Doorman role and the others' Gatekeeper roles appears meaningful: Gerk can directly open doors, while the other Gatekeepers interact with the keystones and gates differently.

plotSections.title: The Gods Depart
bullets: The assembled gods are dismissed after the party's questions. Vecna leaves to find a book and warns the party to have fun with their new abilities but reminds them that they are still mortal.
Ben opens a door from thin air into his traveling tavern and invites the party to return whenever they wish. Mahali follows him and invites them back to the stronghold for a meal.
Narul, the Stranger, gives the party a quiet farewell rather than offering additional information.
Emhet prepares to leave and tells the Gatekeepers that they now hold the keys. Emhet also gives cryptic guidance: if the mind walks, hold your breath and do not yell, and trust the path.

plotSections.title: The Raven Queen's Judgment
bullets: The Raven Queen approaches the party after observing the council. Her appearance resolves from a harpy-like form of black feathers into a slender, regal figure in a dark flowing robe with a blank white porcelain feminine face and owl-like facial detailing.

The Raven Queen acknowledges that the party has opinions about her and that they have seen and done things she could once have judged them for. She accepts that they are mortals and therefore does not hold their past actions against them, while making clear that she would act against them if circumstances warranted it.
She reveals that she was once more mortal and has been to the places the party comes from. She has also seen some of them at the Everfalls, specifically lingering on Sylan and Dana.

She says the party has accomplished more than she expected. She expresses particular confidence in Sylan's ability to fulfill his task, while saying that Walker and Ord have not impressed her greatly but have nevertheless shown her something beyond what she normally sees from mortals.
The Raven Queen offers to lead the party where they need to go, but warns them not to turn the journey into a fool's errand or waste either her time or their own.

She warns the party against treating death casually. She is willing to bargain, noting that lives or opportunities related to death are finite and that some members of the party may not have many chances remaining.
Her final advice is not to defy death, but to make their lives and eventual deaths meaningful: make it a good one and make it something to remember.

chronologicalEvents: Gerk is welcomed as an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Tree.
The party learns that Gerk is the Doorman, while the other members are Gatekeepers; the distinction appears to grant Gerk a different relationship with doors and portals.
Gerk opens an invisible door by reaching for a nonexistent handle, peeling reality back to reveal a beach at sunset somewhere on Midgard.
The DM confirms that Gerk's first door destination cannot currently be selected precisely and was somewhere on a Midgard coastline.
Sylan attempts to use his keystone and briefly senses an invisible opening, but cannot yet open it.
The assembled gods begin departing after the party concludes its questioning.
Vecna leaves to find a book and reminds the party that they remain mortal despite their new powers.
Ben opens a doorway into his traveling tavern and invites the party to return; Mahali follows and invites them to the stronghold for food.
Narul quietly departs without further discussion.
Emhet tells the party that they now hold the keys and gives cryptic instructions concerning the mind walking, holding their breath, remaining silent, and trusting the path.
The Raven Queen approaches and reveals that she has observed the party and has seen some of them at the Everfalls.
The Raven Queen offers to guide the party where they need to go while warning them not to waste time or treat death lightly.
The Raven Queen says she is willing to bargain and warns that some members of the party may have few chances or lives remaining.
The Raven Queen concludes by telling the party not to defy death, but to make their lives and eventual deaths something worth remembering.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian and party ambassador; identified as the Doorman and Child of the Tree.
notes: Gerk is formally welcomed as an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Tree.
Gerk is specifically designated the Doorman, distinct from the party's Gatekeepers.
Gerk can reach forward and grasp an invisible door handle, opening a seamless doorway through reality.
His first opened doorway led to an unknown beach or coastline somewhere on Midgard.
The exact destination of his door could not be determined or selected during this first attempt.
quotesThemes: Gerk embraces the Doorman role and jokingly claims expertise with doors.
openQuestions: Can Gerk eventually choose the destination of a door he opens?

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and one of the party's Gatekeepers.
notes: Sylan is treated as one of the Gatekeepers rather than the Doorman.
When attempting to use his keystone, Sylan briefly felt something in the air before the sensation disappeared.
Sylan believes he needs more time to learn how to use the keystone.

Raven Queen.existing: AKA Nira; god of the dead and an elder god.
notes: The Raven Queen has been observing the party and approaches after the other gods depart.
Her apparent harpy-like form resolves into a slender, regal humanoid figure wearing a dark flowing robe and a blank white porcelain feminine mask with delicate owl-like facial detailing.
She says she was once more mortal and has visited places the party comes from.
She has seen some members of the party at the Everfalls, specifically drawing attention to Sylan and Dana.
She is more impressed by the party's accomplishments than she expected to be.
She offers to lead the party to where they need to go, provided they do not waste her time or turn the journey into a fool's errand.
She is willing to bargain and warns that death is not something to play with.
She implies that some members of the party have limited chances or lives remaining.
She advises the party to make their lives and eventual deaths meaningful rather than trying to defy death.
personality: Cautious, severe, pragmatic, and willing to help when she believes the party's actions are worthwhile.
Views mortality as a finite resource and treats death as something that should be respected rather than casually challenged.
quotesThemes: Death is not something you should play with.
Do not defy death; make it a good one and something to remember.
openQuestions: What exactly does the Raven Queen mean by some party members having few chances or lives remaining?
Why has the Raven Queen seen Sylan and Dana at the Everfalls?

notes: Emhet is a deity present at the council who departs after speaking briefly with the party.
Before leaving, Emhet tells the party that they now hold the keys.
Emhet gives cryptic instructions: if the mind walks, hold your breath and do not yell, and trust the path.
quotesThemes: You now all hold the keys.
openQuestions: What does Emhet mean by 'if the mind walks'?
What path is Emhet referring to?

Vecna.existing: God of liches and an elder god.
notes: Vecna leaves the gathering to find a book.
He reminds the party that despite their new powers and responsibilities, they are still mortal.
quotesThemes: The party's new abilities are toys that should be used carefully because they remain mortal.

Ben.existing: AKA Ballard; minor deity, keeper of the Watchers, and the party's friend who runs the traveling bar.
notes: Ben demonstrates that he can open a doorway from thin air into his traveling tavern.
He tells the party they are welcome whenever they wish and expects to see them again.

Mahali.existing: Elder god and the party's chef.
notes: Mahali follows Ben through the doorway into the traveling tavern.
Mahali invites the party to return to the stronghold and describes a meal of lamb souffles, cabbage stew, and cherry or lemon curd.

Narul.existing: AKA the Stranger; elder god and former god of death.
notes: Narul silently gives the party a nod, forehead gesture, and slight bow before departing.
Narul does not provide additional information before leaving.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and one of the party's Gatekeepers.
notes: Dana tells Emhet that her questions have been answered for now and that he will hear her prayers if she needs further guidance.
The Raven Queen specifically focuses on Dana while mentioning that she has seen some of the party at the Everfalls.
openQuestions: What did the Raven Queen see Dana doing at the Everfalls?

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; one of the party's Gatekeepers.
notes: The Raven Queen specifically evaluates Walker and Ord and says they have not impressed her as much as some others, although they have still shown her something beyond what she normally sees from mortals.

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin; one of the party's Gatekeepers.
notes: The Raven Queen specifically evaluates Ord and Walker and says they have not impressed her as much as some others, although they have still shown her something beyond what she normally sees from mortals.
Kit Anger welcomes the newly recognized Child of the Tree with a slap on the back.

Navi.existing: Ancient race associated with the Eldarin Tree and the creation of the keystones.
notes: Gerk is explicitly welcomed as an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Tree.
Gerk is explicitly welcomed as a Child of the Tree.
The title represents a connection to the Navi and the sacred tree associated with the keystones.
Gerk's role is explicitly distinguished from the Gatekeepers.
The Doorman can open a door directly through reality, demonstrated when Gerk created a doorway to a Midgard beach.
openQuestions: What other abilities or responsibilities are unique to the Doorman?

notes: The party members other than Gerk are referred to as Gatekeepers.
Emhet confirms that the Gatekeepers now hold the keys.
The Gatekeeper role appears to involve interacting with the keystones and the paths between realms.
openQuestions: How does the Gatekeeper role differ mechanically or magically from the Doorman?

notes: The Raven Queen says she has seen some of the party at the Everfalls, specifically drawing attention to Sylan and Dana.
openQuestions: What exactly did the Raven Queen witness at the Everfalls?

notes: Emhet gives the party cryptic instructions that if the mind walks, they should hold their breath and not yell.
The instruction appears to be connected to safely traveling along a path or gate.
openQuestions: What is a mind walk and how does it relate to the gates?

misTranscriptions.notes: The transcript repeatedly renders Sylan's name as variants such as 'Silen,' 'Silin,' and 'silent,' including when the context clearly concerns the known party rogue.
The DM appears to address Gerk, but the ASR renders the name as 'Lynn' during the discussion of who summoned the gods.
The DM appears to be talking about dismissing the assembled gods, but the transcript renders 'gods' as 'cards.'
The term is already canonical, but the surrounding sentence should be interpreted as Walker asking whether the gods have anything else to say about Grixto.
This appears to be a previously unlisted deity or NPC name; retain as Emhet unless campaign notes establish another spelling.
Likely a specific campaign concept or magical travel term rather than ordinary phrasing, but its exact meaning is unclear.

openQuestions: Can Gerk choose where his Doorman doors lead, or are destinations initially random or uncontrolled?
What is the precise distinction between the Doorman and the Gatekeepers?
What does Emhet mean by 'if the mind walks, hold your breath'?
What does it mean to 'trust the path'?
What did the Raven Queen witness involving Sylan and Dana at the Everfalls?

newTerms.name: Doorman
notes: Gerk's unique role among the newly empowered party; allows him to open doors directly through reality.
Distinct from the Gatekeeper role held by the other party members.

newTerms.name: Gatekeeper
notes: Role assigned to the other party members in contrast to Gerk's Doorman role.
Gatekeepers now hold the keys and are expected to interact with the paths and gates between realms.

newTerms.name: Child of the Tree
notes: A title associated with becoming an honorary member of the Navi.
Gerk is explicitly welcomed as a Child of the Tree in this scene.

newTerms.name: Mind Walk
notes: A cryptic concept referenced by Emhet in instructions about holding one's breath and not yelling.

newTerms.name: Everfalls
notes: A location where the Raven Queen says she has previously seen members of the party, specifically Sylan and Dana.
